incidents.name: Apollo 1
incidents.what_happened: A flash fire swept through the cabin, pressurized with 100 % oxygen, during a ground test. The three crew died of asphyxia from carbon monoxide and toxic gases; their burns were likely survivable.
incidents.cause: Likely ignition from arcing wires near the environmental control system; pure oxygen made the fire spread very fast.
lessons: Strictly control the amount and location of combustible materials
A hatch that opens in 3 seconds
incidents.connection: Material flammability limits at high oxygen (BASS, BASS-II, Saffire) and the high-O2 flame data of CFI-G address exactly the risk Apollo 1 exposed.

incidents.name: Apollo 13
incidents.setting: Service Module oxygen tank, en route to the Moon
incidents.what_happened: Oxygen tank 2 exploded, damaging tank 1; the crew used the Lunar Module as a lifeboat and returned safely.
incidents.cause: Heater thermostats were not upgraded for a 65 V supply; heaters overheated to about 1000 F and degraded the wire insulation inside an oxygen tank.
lessons: Redesign oxygen storage and review all cryogenic-oxygen systems
Insulation added after Apollo 1 prevented arcing at re-entry power-up
incidents.connection: Overheated insulation in an oxygen-rich space is a pre-fire event: SAME/SAME-R show that detecting pyrolysis products early is the key to catching it.

incidents.name: Mir station fire
incidents.what_happened: A solid-fuel oxygen generator canister ignited, shooting a ~1 m flame that blocked the path to a Soyuz escape craft and filled the station with smoke. Foam extinguishers were used; the flame burned out on its own.
incidents.cause: Most likely latex glove material contaminated the lithium-perchlorate canister.
lessons: Changed crew emergency training and ground support
Changed ground preparation of oxygen canisters
Redundant, dissimilar oxygen generation on ISS
incidents.connection: Suppression in microgravity (FLEX, BASS) and smoke behaviour and detection (SAME, DAFT) are the research areas this fire made urgent.

incidents.name: Artemis II smoke alarm
incidents.what_happened: A smoke alarm went off during the crewed lunar flyby, a reminder that any alarm far from home demands immediate, reliable answers.
incidents.cause: Reported in the challenge statement; details not covered in the provided resources.
lessons: Detectors must be sensitive yet resistant to false alarms on long missions
incidents.connection: SAME, SAME-R and DAFT characterize smoke versus background dust so detectors raise fewer false alarms.

myths.myth: A steady fire cannot exist in still microgravity air.
myths.reality: Candle flames burned for over 45 minutes on Mir, and flame balls burned for 40+ minutes in space.

myths.myth: A fire will self-extinguish if the ventilation is shut off.
myths.reality: A local suppressant jet entrains air and sustains the flame even with ambient airflow off.

myths.myth: Earth-gravity fire tests are conservative for space.
myths.reality: BASS showed materials can burn at lower oxygen in microgravity; NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 is not conservative.

myths.myth: Inert-gas suppressants work as well in space as on Earth.
myths.reality: FLEX found a lower limiting oxygen index in reduced gravity, so Earth standards give less safety margin.

myths.myth: Earth smoke detectors will work in a spacecraft.
myths.reality: Microgravity smoke particles differ in size; detectors must look for different signatures, especially pre-fire pyrolysis products.
myths.source: Researcher's Guide, p. 35; SAME fact sheet

spinoffs.name: Lighter firefighter air tanks
spinoffs.detail: Spacesuit-derived breathing system: 20 lb with 30 minutes of air, 13 lb lighter than conventional tanks, pressurized to 4,500 psi.

spinoffs.name: Incipient fire detector
spinoffs.detail: Shuttle detector that senses fire before flame or smoke and tells combustion particles from dust; trialled in mining.

spinoffs.name: FIRES firefighter gear
spinoffs.detail: Fire-resistant suit materials from Apollo (e.g. PBI, developed after the Apollo 1 fire) cut ensemble weight by about 40 %.

spinoffs.name: Water-mist extinguishers
spinoffs.detail: Portable water-mist extinguishers developed from microgravity mist research replaced CO2 units on the ISS, with uses on Earth.

spinoffs.name: Submarine and habitat smoke detection
spinoffs.detail: SAME results inform smoke detectors for submarines and underwater laboratories.

gaps.title: No partial-gravity data yet
gaps.detail: PSI holds microgravity (and some 1-g comparison) data only. Lunar and Martian habitats must be bounded between them until FM2 and LUCI report.

gaps.title: Few tests at lunar-habitat atmospheres
gaps.detail: Only gas-flame and droplet studies (FLEX, BRE, CFI-G, Flame Design) reach 30-40 % O2; the highest oxygen any solid material was burned at in PSI is 22.2 % (BASS-II).

gaps.title: Pure-oxygen suit conditions
gaps.detail: The highest O2 in PSI is ~85 % in inverse gas flames; nothing approaches 100 % O2 at 4.3 psi.

gaps.title: Suppression of solid fires
gaps.detail: Suppression data are mostly droplets (FLEX) and small nitrogen jets (BASS); water mist and large-fire suppression are not in PSI.
